text:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector change I'm seeing weird tail latency on Mixtral small-batch workloads. basic summary: 99th latency up ~35% on 2k request sample.

maria: Ugh. Any reproducible profile? Is it only Mixtral or others too?

dave: Saw a smaller bump on Llama too but Mixtral/MQA seems worst. Could be KV layout + kernel choice mismatch.

elaine: I ran a quick perf-ci trace: flamegraph shows a big chunk in gpu memcpy and kernel launch overhead when num_key_value_heads != attention_heads. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/174900

alex: Repro steps I used: 
```
perf run --model=mixtral-8b-mqa --seq=512 --batch=1 --mode=latency --kv-cache=paged --threads=1
```
Result: P95 ~48ms -> 65ms after selector change. P99 similar jump.

maria: That command uses paged KV cache; paging fragmentation increases memcpy count when KV dims are packed per-head. If kernel selector swapped to a pack-optimized kernel that expects contiguous KV, paged layout leads to scatter/gather copies.

elaine: Exactly. The new kernel picks the 'pack-concat' path for Mixtral because of reported head dims, but our paged-KV layout is head-strided and causes extra kernels to reformat.

alex: So two levers: (1) change kernel selection to prefer 'strided-kv' kernels for paged layout, (2) change paged-KV allocator to blend heads into fewer pages (reduce fragmentation).

dave: On model-specific notes: Mixtral sets num_key_value_heads=32 vs attention_heads=32, but kv_dim per head is 64. Qwen uses kv_dim 128 and often MQA where kv_heads != attn_heads. RoPE scaling also differs — Qwen uses RoPE scaling factor that increases effective sequence dim. That affects kernel tiling and launch sizes.

maria: Also saw RoPE scaling impact on perf: when we apply 1.5x RoPE scaling on Qwen, the attention kernel's occupancy drops because effective sequence math uses different vector sizes -> integer division causes extra padding in tiled matmuls. Explains increased memory traffic.

elaine: From the profiler: hotspot order: 1) KV pack/unpack kernels 2) attention GEMM + softmax 3) memcpy for paged KV 4) kernel launch overhead. For Mixtral-MQA the pack/unpack step doubled.

alex: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert kernel selector change for models flagged as paged-KV or with mismatch in kv_heads vs attn_heads. Add unit test in selector that simulates paged layout cost.

maria: I can add a heuristic: if paged_kv_enabled && (num_kv_heads != attn_heads || kv_dim % 64 != 0) then prefer 'strided-kv' kernel. Tight but should avoid perf cliff.

dave: Longer term: consider a per-model kernel table produced at onboarding time. We run a micro-benchmark for MQA/GQA variants and record the fastest kernel+layout combo. That avoids brittle heuristics.

elaine: +1. Also add a tiny allocator change: try coalescing small head pages into larger pages when memory pressure low — trades a bit of commit complexity for fewer memcpy ops. I have a prototype patch.

alex: Any quick experiments we can run to confirm?

elaine: Patch 1: selector revert, Patch 2: allocator coalesce. I ran locally with both: P99 back to 47ms, P95 44ms. So looks promising. I pushed a perf-ci run: https://perf.redwood/internal/run/174900-2

maria: Can you paste the allocator diff or config? Even a runtime flag would be nice.

elaine: Config snippet I used: 
```
kv_paging:
  enabled: true
  coalesce_threshold: 3   # merge <=3 small head pages into one page
  page_size_kb: 64
```

alex: Nice. Any regressions on long sequences / high batch throughput? Coalescing could increase page reuse and reduce cache eviction at large seqs.

elaine: I ran a throughput job seq=2048 batch=8 — no regression, actually slight improvement in throughput (2-3%) due to fewer format kernels. But memory footprint increased ~1.7%.

maria: Memory tradeoff is acceptable for Dedicated customers. For hosted, we should gate coalesce behind a config per-deployment tier.

dave: About RoPE scaling — could we auto-select tile sizes in GEMM kernels based on rope_scale? We already pass seq_len and kv_dim to kernel planner; add rope_scale to planner heuristic.

alex: Good idea. Planner change: estimate padded_kv_dim = ceil(kv_dim * rope_scale / tile) * tile and choose tile minimizing padding overhead. We can store this result per-model.

elaine: One more observation: the perf regression surfaced mostly on short sequences (<=64). For longer sequences the batching heuristics overshadowed kernel cost. So we should tweak batching heuristics: prefer batching multiple short requests to reach GPU-friendly batch size before firing tiny kernels.

maria: We already have an adaptive batching window; maybe lower timeout for short-reqs but allow bundling up to N requests if tail-latency impact small. Propose: if seq<=64 and model in MQA family, max_bundle=4.

alex: Let's action items: 
- elaine: open PR for selector revert + unit test (urgent)
- elaine: PR for allocator coalesce config (staged rollout)
- maria: add rope_scale to kernel planner and include in per-model benchmark harness
- dave: run cluster-wide perf job for Mixtral/Qwen/Llama variants with patched selector+coalesce
- alex: draft rollout plan + host gating for coalesce

elaine: I'll have the two PRs in review by EOD. Perf-ci run already passing smoke.

perf-ci-bot: perf run complete for job 174900-2 — diff summary: mixtral-8b-mqa p99 -18%, average latency -12%, memory +1.7% (coalesce on).

maria: Thanks. Once PRs merge let's schedule a canary on Dedicated clusters and monitor token-level latency traces.

alex: Perfect. Also add an alert for sudden increases in memcpy/kernel-format time in the flamegraphs — that's a good early signal for future selector changes.

dave: I'll draft the per-model micro-benchmark harness and add results to model onboarding docs.

alex: Great work team. 

maria: :thumbsup:

elaine: cc @ops to watch canary slots tomorrow morning.

ops: noted — will monitor the 3 canaries starting 09:00 PT.
